title: vulnflow machines.toml
description: Your hosts, code, GitHub repositories and asset context. Generated by `vulnflow schema`; see machines.example.toml.

groups.description: Shared settings plus the hosts in them. Never exposure or criticality: one group can run a public service and an internal admin page.

scans.description: What the agent scans (default: system on linux; brew, languages, apps on macos).

language_paths.description: Extra language tool directories, relative to $HOME.

containers_team.description: Owner of the container projects (default dev).

hosts.description: Per-host settings and asset context of the host project.

scans.description: What the agent scans (default: system on linux; brew, languages, apps on macos).

language_paths.description: Extra language tool directories, relative to $HOME.

containers_team.description: Owner of the container projects (default dev).

exposure.description:
Who can reach it (docs/exposure.md). Empty = unknown.

- `internet`: reachable by anyone on the internet, before login
- `external-auth`: reachable from outside, but only after login
- `internal`: reachable from the internal network or user devices
- `restricted`: segmented, admin-only, allow-listed (e.g. tailnet only)
- `hostile-device`: runs on devices the organisation does not control

input.description:
Who controls the input it parses. Empty = unknown.

- `public`: anyone can supply input
- `partner`: known external parties
- `staff`: employees only

criticality.description:
How much it matters. Empty = unknown.

- `critical`: harm to the public, customers or society
- `high`: the organisation cannot do its core work
- `normal`: everything else
- `low`: test, sandbox, decommissioning

review.description: eol/certified only: when the accepted risk is looked at again (YYYY-MM-DD); the weekly report flags it once passed.

group.description: Join a group without being in its hosts list.

images.description: Asset context of the container projects on this host, by image name, its last part, or a glob; `"*"` catches the rest.

chat.description: Mattermost channels for noisy products (the Linux kernel, a chatty vendor). Alerts for them go there instead of the team's channel; `./poc.sh chat-up` creates the channel and its webhook.

min_tier.description: Lowest tier posted (default: the team channel's, P2).

news.description: Per-team OSINT newsletter (`vulnflow newsletter`): feeds and where each team's newsletter goes.

feeds.description: RSS, Atom or JSON Feed URLs, downloaded whole and filtered locally (never searched per keyword).

kind.description: advisory, cert, exploit (items count as a public exploit) or news.

teams.description: Send every item to these teams; empty: match each item against every team.

to.description: E-mail address for this team's newsletter.

keywords.description: Extra words to match in feed items.

cpe_map.description: Formula, cask or bundle id -> NVD vendor:product.
